title: Custom Difficulty Slider Range
doc: CKF Hard Mode - custom-difficulty slider range.
One setting. It widens the Min/Max bounds of the game's own
custom-difficulty sliders so they reach further; the difficulty itself
is set in the game's window.
GameDifficultyModel's bound properties are static, not per-row data [measured:
a materialized row carries 66 instance properties and no bound], so
widening is a one-shot on the type at load. The reconfigure and
materializer hooks re-run it; every bound is computed from the stock
value captured the first time, so re-running does not compound.
[PowerLevel] is unaffected by this section. It reads the model
properties the sliders write, so it picks up whatever was set in-game.
uiDoc: This does not set difficulty. It widens how far the game's own custom difficulty sliders can be pushed. You then set the difficulty itself in the game's own window.
A ceiling is multiplied outward. A floor above zero is pulled closer to zero. A floor already below zero is pushed further down. A limit of exactly zero is left where it is.

fields.label: Enable Custom Difficulty Slider Range
fields.doc: Slice toggle, read in Plugin.Load. Off: the sliders keep their stock bounds and nothing is patched. It lives in ckf.hardmode.cfg because a gate cannot live inside the file it gates. Slices.Init binds every [Slices] key above the [General] Enabled bail-out, so BepInEx writes the line even when the mod is off; a key that cannot be read is reported at Error and treated as on. difficulty.json has no retired "enabled" key. The subsystem is also skipped, with an Error, when GameDifficultyModel does not resolve.
fields.uiDoc: Turn this off and this part of the mod does nothing; the game uses its own values. The master switch on the first page turns off everything at once.

fields.label: Slider range multiplier
fields.doc: How far past stock the game's own custom-difficulty sliders may be pushed. GameDifficultyModel pairs each setting with writable Min/Max properties, so this stretches them: a positive ceiling is multiplied, a negative floor is multiplied (further down), a positive floor is divided (closer to zero), and a bound of exactly zero is left alone. 1 = leave the stock ranges alone, which is also what happens when difficulty.json cannot be read.
